messages:
maria: quick report from a user trying our quickstart on Vercel Edge: their TypeScript build errors with weird `any` leaking when calling `client.chat.create` with a `parse` callback. works fine in node but not in the edge bundle. _devrel: can you paste the error and the callsite? Vite + esbuild often changes resolution. maria: error: `TS2345: Argument of type '(s: string) => T' is not assignable to parameter of type '(s: string) => unknown'` and a bunch of inferred `any` on downstream vars. callsite is like:```ts const result = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-v1', parse: (s)=>JSON.parse(s) }); // expect result to be any/unknown or parsed value, but inference is lost ``` _leo: what's our declaration for chat.create? overloads? generic? maria: our types:```ts export function create(opts: { model: string }): Promise; export function create(opts: { model: string; parse: (s: string) => T }): Promise; ``` _anya: overloads like that can be brittle when TS resolves to the .d.ts that matches the ESM path. bundlers sometimes prefer consuming `types` from a different entry, and inference picks the first overload which returns `string`. _maria: the twist: user's package.json has `type: module`, Vite picks the ESM entry and the ESM .d.ts we ship has slightly different ordering (we re-export types from internal index). so resolution leads to the non-generic overload being picked. _devrel: options: 1) collapse to single generic with default `unknown` 2) add a generic overload first (so inference hits it) 3) provide a safer wrapper `parseJson(s: string): T` to force explicitness. _leo: also consider changing our published `.d.ts` to use a single exported signature that uses conditional types to infer parse result:```ts export function create

(opts: P extends { parse: (s: string)=>infer R } ? { model: string; parse: (s: string)=>R } : { model: string }): Promise

infer R } ? R : string>; ``` _anya: that conditional looks clever but may be too obscure for users and long compile times. simpler: `export function create(opts: { model: string; parse?: (s: string)=>T }): Promise;` then document that default is string. _maria: another immediate fix is to publish per-entry types in `exports` so ESM consumers see the same d.ts shape as CJS. example package.json:```json "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts" } }, "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts", "typesVersions": {"*": {"*": ["dist/esm/*"]}} ``` _devrel: good call. also add a small repro that runs `tsc --noEmit` with `moduleResolution: bundler` and `module: ES2022` like Vite uses. add to quickstart CI matrix. _leo: for the short term we should also change the sample's tsconfig to avoid `skipLibCheck` hacks and instead demonstrate the `moduleResolution` tweak and note `type: module` caveats in the readme. users hit this during onboarding and it's a big friction. _build-bot: build / sample-quickstart / typecheck failed on branch fix-typing (see logs): https://ci/redwood/789/logs :x: _maria: i'm going to open a small PR that: 1) replaces overloads with single-generic default, 2) updates package exports to include `types` on the import entry, 3) adds CI tsc job with Vite-like tsconfigs, 4) docs note about `type: module` and how bundlers pick d.ts. _anya: if you want i can review the conditional-typing approach vs explicit generic docs. would love to avoid confusing users but still keep ergonomics. _maria: thanks — PR inbound. i'll drop a minimal repro repo in the thread so folks can run local checks. also calling out the edge target (Vercel worker, Cloudflare) in the test matrix. _devrel: after PR let's roll a beta patch and publish it so quickstart points at the fixed version. onboarding NPS should go up :) _maria: agreed. keeping this thread as the tracker. feel free to ping me if you want to pair on the repro. :shipit:
